title: English bands and the tour of England
summary: Robinson praises English bands, describes arrival in London and warm hospitality there and in New York.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What do you think about those English bands? Good bands. What bands do you like over in England in particular?

Kid got a good band. I was over there. Ken Cut. And this Booyah got a good band too. They call him Trummelbill. You know him? Oh. Oh. Oh. Kid's over here. You know there are a couple of good lads here. Chris Barber. Oh yeah. Chris got a good band dude. He played all them bands on concert. He played all them bands on concert.

Yeah, they bought some fine colors. And every Sydney winter, you know what I mean? They had a band at the train, at the airplane. Oh yeah? Every Sydney winter. Yeah. Nice people. In London, we got there Sunday. We were in Liverpool one night at the hotels. The next morning we got the train. That evening we got in London that evening around about 2 o'clock. Oh man, they thought it was some kind of big convention. People had the train. The shade, just stand up on the shades of the airport. The shade went down. King Collier had his brass band there playing. Got a good bass band too. Really nice fellas. I would like to make a little trip over there. People, I'm telling you it's true. You know, make a man feel different, you know. People like that so, they're so nice, polite to you. You understand?

Mm-hmm. But what about people in New York? Are they like that? People in New York is nice people too. Because, you see, but see Dick, I'll tell you one thing. Like a musician like us, we got, we had such a chance to give the best part to people.

That makes a thing too in effect. Now, if we had to, if I went to the world, they were going to fight, they get, I think people are bad too. But see, I can't say that for people. Because when I, we often say that, the people, they take us around and feel so nice. And I can't say you know bad fella and listen and that about you. But see, it's what I think of the man. The people really nice.

Because any time he goes out in the way, we can't put a nickel. No way. Take us to the house. We eat. Understand? We eat. If it's necessary, they got a room there. You know what I'm saying? You don't want to run to sleep, you know what I'm saying? Rest. You see? Man can't, man can't have no bed than that.
